heading: INT. DUMPLING KITCHEN - BACK TABLE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. DUMPLING KITCHEN - BACK TABLE - NIGHT
Steam curls from bamboo baskets.
A wall of orange tiles, a radio murmuring in Cantonese.
Four people crowd a stainless counter, pleating dumplings by hand.
CELESTE MARCHAND, 30s, silk blouse, sleeves rolled, pleats each one with great concentration.
RORY BANERJEE, 30s, sits across from her, flour on his glasses.
NONNA LUCIA, 80s, wiry, in a faded apron, oversees them with a wooden spoon.
TOMASZ WISNIEWSKI, 50s, the chef, passes behind with a tray, wiping his hands on his hip.
Too much filling. You will burst them.
units.name: NONNA LUCIA

units.text: I like them fat.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: She does.
units.name: RORY

units.text: Celeste's hands pause.
She doesn't look up.
He reaches for a wrapper, their fingers brush the flour, and neither of them moves for a beat.
Everyone eat! Plates are coming!
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: You. You are the one from the letters.
units.name: NONNA LUCIA

units.text: Which letters?
units.name: RORY

units.text: The ones she does not send.
units.name: NONNA LUCIA

units.text: Celeste drops a dumpling.
It lands on the tile with a wet slap.
Tomasz glides by and stoops to retrieve it, humming.
Okay.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Celeste--
units.name: RORY

units.text: It's fine. Tell Tomasz the soy is low.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: She stands, wipes her hands, and walks out through the swinging door.
Rory watches it swing.
Nonna Lucia pats the empty chair.
Sit. Pleat. It is always better in the second hour.
units.name: NONNA LUCIA
